# Drafter notes — cid-tiradas-137-137a

28 units, 68 verses (3060–3126 incl. Pidal's own 3114b), all tirada 137 (which runs on into the next part).
`t` cut by script from packet.md (scratchpad build_units.py: units given as first/last verse number, `t` =
packet lines joined by "\n", numbers stripped). Asserted in the script: units cover every packet verse once, in
order; `l` line count = `t` line count for each unit. JSON parses. titleEn/part with the default name, "Cid"
without cedilla in the title; "Tirada 137 (first part)" in `part`, as the tirada continues.

Rubric of 137 read on PDF 321 (printed 317): only the first three clauses (preparation at San Servando; goes to
Toledo and enters the court; the king offers his bench, the Cid declines) folded into the first note, with
"continues in the next part".

Footnotes read on the scan (PDF 321–325) and quoted Spanish + English in the notes: 3070, 3073, 3080, 3085,
3086, 3087, 3088, 3089, 3090, 3091, 3092, 3094, 3096, 3097, 3098, 3099, 3105, 3112, 3115, 3116, 3121, 3124.
(3058-59 run-on belongs to the last part; 3130 to the next.) Paragraph indents seen at 3084, 3101, 3104, 3114
— said in the notes for 3084, 3101, 3104.

## Readings for the reviewer to check
1. **3063 "mejor."** full stop inside the speech before small "vos": kept, said in the note; sense runs on.
2. **3094 "pro,"**: the mark is damaged (a dot with something beneath, seen at zoom 5); read as comma, the
   sense running on to 3095–96. Said in the note.
3. **3100 ve[er] / el[le]** and **3114b se[er]**: checked at zoom 4: "ve"/"se" roman, "er" italic; "el" roman,
   "le" italic. Agrees with the pinned text. 3118 se[e]d: the second e italic, agrees.
4. **3107 "naçió." before small "levantós"**: kept; note says the sentence runs on, possibly a misprint for a comma.
5. **3103 "mio Cid"** without cedilla: kept as printed; "my Çid" in `i`.
6. **3116 âlgunos** = a + algunos (house circumflex).
7. **3114**: a mio and the whole second half-line restored by Pidal; colon after Çid kept; rendered
   "The king took my Çid by the hands". No footnote of Pidal's on it.
8. **3062 [a sazón]** (wholly Pidal's, no footnote): "duly given / in season" is our reading.
9. **3061 suelta**: 'finished' — our reading of the participle, said so.
10. **3077 dulçes** of swords: 'fine-tempered' — our reading, said so (no Pidal note here).
11. **3080 desobra**: Pidal 'demasía, desmán' (voz desconocida) → "trouble/outrage", uncertain.
12. **3088 presa** ('presilla' (?)) and **3089 ca él se lo mandó** (?): both carry Pidal's own query; followed
    with the uncertainty stated; 3089 rendered after Adam.
13. **3091 pareçen por o son**: Bello's reading via Pidal (huebras understood from obrado); o = 'where'.
14. **3092 bandas**: Pidal's 'more natural' 'franja' followed → "bands".
15. **3095 fecha por razón**: "made for a purpose" — our reading.
16. **3096 contalassen**: Pidal's guess ('arrancar', verbo desconocido) followed.
17. **3098 recabdar**: Pidal gives two senses (Bello 'lograr' / Hinard 'prevenir'); "secure" chosen to cover both;
    flagged.
18. **3097 note reference "p. 119, n."**: printed with a small subscript figure (19 or 10) after 119; not clear.
19. **3112 Crespo de Grañón**: "the Curly-haired of Grañón", as in 134-136; Pidal identifies García Ordóñez.
20. **3109 Remont** (spelt with t here): "Count Remond" (house).
21. **3068 nació** without cedilla, as in the packet (naçió elsewhere) — not checked on the scan beyond zoom 1.4,
    where it looks cedilla-less.

Note: page.py needs PyMuPDF; in this environment it ran only under /usr/local/bin/python3.13 (python3 is 3.11).
